newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Around 150 Kabila supporters march in Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Around 150 Kabila supporters march in Kinshasa.

text.p: A group of around 150 supporters of self-proclaimed President Laurent Kabila marched down the main street of Kinshasa on Saturday after troops broke up an anti-Kabila student march, witnesses said.

The witnesses said the marchers, many of whom were followers of murdered independence prime minister Patrice Lumumba, called on people of Kinshasa to support Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL).
Kabila's troops entered Kinshasa a week ago after a seven month war to end the 32-year reign of president Mobutu Sese Seko, who is now in Morocco.

AFDL soldiers earlier stopped a demonstration of around 1,000 students protesting about Kabila's exclusion of popular opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi from the new government and the presence of Rwandan troops.

"Hardly installed in office, Kabila's government is already attacked by the same dinosaurs thirsty for power who failed to get rid of Mobutu. Support the AFDL, fight for the motherland," said a leaflet handed out by the pro-Kabila marchers.
Troops allowed the march to proceed peacefully, and foreign journalists who had their film of the student march confiscated were allowed to film.
Despite the rival demonstrations it was business as usual in Kinshasa. Shops were open and traffic circulated normally.
But many people said they were concerned at the new turn of events in the capital and said that calm was more important than other considerations.
"All we want is peace," said one bystander as the student demonstration passed.

Witnesses said the pro-Kabila marchers were largely members of the National Movement of Congo (MNC) of Lambert Mende, a minister in Mobutu's last civilian government under prime minister Kengo wa Dondo.
